In this work's scherzo, timpani play a prominent role, and the finale begins with a recitative for cellos and basses that rejects earlier themes. The finale sets lines by Friedrich Schiller for four vocal soloists and chorus. It premiered in Vienna in 1824, with its deaf composer on stage. For 10 points, name this symphony in D minor whose "Ode to Joy" became the anthem of the European Union.

Lutherans teach that Christ is present in, with, and under the bread and wine, a view often called by this term. Zwingli instead argued for a purely symbolic meaning at the 1529 Marburg Colloquy. For 10 points, give this Latin-based term for the Lord's Supper, also called Communion.

This signaling molecule's cyclic form, abbreviated cAMP, was discovered by Earl Sutherland as a second messenger. It is produced from ATP by adenylyl cyclase after a G protein-coupled receptor is activated. For 10 points, name this second messenger that activates protein kinase A.

This graph traversal algorithm extends a shortest-path method by adding a heuristic estimate of the remaining distance to the goal, ordering nodes by the sum of cost so far and that estimate. It is optimal if the heuristic never overestimates. It was developed at the Stanford Research Institute for the robot Shakey. For 10 points, name this pathfinding algorithm commonly used in video games, whose name is a letter followed by a punctuation symbol.
